subject: Proposed MAP + evaluation timeline and commercial options for GlobalRetail pilot
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@globalretail.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 12:15:00 +0000
Subject: Proposed MAP + evaluation timeline and commercial options for GlobalRetail pilot

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the time earlier. As discussed, I’m sharing a proposed mutual action plan (MAP) and evaluation timeline for the pilot so we can align milestones to commercial triggers. Attached: GlobalRetail-MAP-v1.xlsx and a draft SOW for scope. TL;DR below.

Overview (90-day pilot, EU data residency):
- Week 0–2: Onboarding & networking (VPC connect, KMS integration)
- Week 3–6: Eval workload (2 production-like flows, 100k tokens/day peak)
- Week 7–10: Performance tuning and KV-prefix caching validation
- Week 11–12: Final QoQ eval, success criteria review and handoff to procurement

Commercial guardrails tied to MAP milestones:
- Pricing baseline: hosted API rates (see sheet).
- Data residency premium (EU region): standard premium = 12% on host rates — applied when full EU data residency (log retention and model inference in EU) is required.
- Ramp & commit discounts: 3-tier discounts on commit (monthly committed vCPU/GPU-hour equivalent) tied to a signed reserved contract at pilot close.
- Cross-region failover: optional add-on (flat monthly fee) to enable automatic failover into a secondary region + cross-region KV replication.

What we want to align on now:
1) Which commercial option do you want priced in the review: baseline + 12% residency premium, or a model where residency premium is reduced in exchange for a 12-month committed ramp?
2) Do you need cross-region failover enabled during the pilot or only in production?
3) Procurement timeline — can we aim to have an executed reserved contract within 30 days of pilot acceptance?

Next steps: Please review the attached MAP and let me know preferred commercial option and any procurement constraints. Happy to hop on a 30-min call tomorrow to walk through the SOW and timelines.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0132

Attachments: GlobalRetail-MAP-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), SOW-draft-GlobalRetail.pdf (PDF)

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@globalretail.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Andrew Simms <andrew.simms@globalretail.com>, procurement@globalretail.com
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 16:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Proposed MAP + evaluation timeline and commercial options for GlobalRetail pilot

Karthik —

Thanks for sending this over and for the clear MAP. A few clarifying questions from my side and procurement:

1) The 12% residency premium — can you explain exactly what drives that (eg storage, logging, dedicated infra)? Are there ways to reduce it if we can accept limited logging retention or keep only inference residency?
2) Cross-region failover: procurement is concerned about the flat monthly fee model. If we only need failover for DR testing twice a year, can that be scoped as a time-limited feature rather than an always-on charge?
3) Pilot end date: can we compress the timeline by one week? We have a board review on Oct 8 and would like results before then.
4) We will need SOC2 and evidence of EU data controls for procurement.

Please mark in the MAP the cost delta for the residency premium and the failover add-on so procurement can run the TCO quickly.

–Elena
Elena Rossi
VP, Cloud & Data Platforms, GlobalRetail
elena.rossi@globalretail.com

To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 15:45:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Proposed MAP + evaluation timeline and commercial options for GlobalRetail pilot

Folks — forwarding Elena’s reply. Key asks:
- Explain drivers of 12% EU residency premium and whether we can reduce it with constrained logging/retention.
- Consider failover as time-limited vs always-on — procurement bargaining point.
- They want one-week compression of pilot; board review Oct 8.
- They asked for SOC2 and EU evidence.

Quick asks: can pricing desk draft 2 alternate commercial options (A: reduce residency premium to 8% with 12-mo commit + ramp schedule; B: 6% premium + 10% credit applied to first 3 months with a shorter commitment) and a proposal for failover charging (included for 90 days during onboarding vs flat monthly fee afterwards)?

I’ve attached the external thread for context. Planning to respond with options + updated MAP.

Thanks — Karthik

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 13 Sep 2026 09:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Proposed MAP + evaluation timeline and commercial options for GlobalRetail pilot

Karthik / team —

Draft commercial compromise below (happy to iterate):

Option A (preferred — recommended by pricing):
- Residency premium: 8% (reduced from 12%) if customer signs a 12-month reserved commitment within 30 days of pilot acceptance.
- Ramp schedule: 30% of committed capacity month 1, 60% month 2, 100% month 3. Discount tiers apply once committed spend thresholds hit.
- Cross-region failover: included at no charge for the first 90 days (covers pilot + stabilization). After that, option to continue as a paid add-on at 9,500 EUR/month or an equivalently priced usage-based fee.
- SOC2 and EU controls: provide SOC2 report and data processing addendum; KMS/HSM evidence can be produced for procurement.

Option B (alternate):
- Residency premium: 6% with a 3-month trial credit equal to 10% of billed usage applied to first 3 months; requires signed 6-month commitment.
- Cross-region failover: charged as a monthly add-on from day 1 at 7,500 EUR/month.

Notes:
- If they insist on no long-term commit, pricing desk will not reduce the residency premium below 10%.
- If they need pilot compressed by one week we can tighten the tuning window but will require additional test engineers during weeks 3–6. That will absorb some onboarding slack; recommend we include a one-time professional services line in the SOW if they compress the schedule.

I’ll draft the revised MAP and a pricing-options CSV. Suggest we present Options A and B to Elena and indicate pricing desk preference for A.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Head of Deal Strategy, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@globalretail.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, procurement@globalretail.com
Date: Sun, 13 Sep 2026 11:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Proposed MAP + evaluation timeline and commercial options for GlobalRetail pilot

Elena —

Appreciate the quick feedback. Based on our internal pricing discussion we can present two concrete options and a recommended path: see attached pricing-options-20260913.csv and an updated MAP (GlobalRetail-MAP-v2.xlsx, linked). Short summary below — please indicate which option you prefer and whether you want failover enabled during the pilot.

Option A (Pricing team recommended):
- Residency premium: 8% (applies when full EU residency is required).
- Commit: 12-month reserved contract to be signed within 30 days of pilot acceptance. Ramp schedule included in MAP.
- Cross-region failover: included free for first 90 days (pilot + stabilization); then 9,500 EUR/month if continued.
- Accelerated schedule: we can compress the MAP by one week but will add a one-time PS line in SOW to cover extra tuning resources.

Option B (Lower commitment):
- Residency premium: 6% with a 10% usage credit applied across months 1–3. Requires a 6-month commitment.
- Cross-region failover: charged from day 1 at 7,500 EUR/month.

Security artifacts: SOC2 report link and EU data controls documentation are available here: https://redwood.ai/security/soc2-report-2026 and we will include the DPA in the SOW.

If you’re comfortable, I can schedule a 30-min call Monday to walk through the MAP+pricing and get procurement set up for signatures (DocuSign link will be provided once you select an option).

Next steps (suggested):
1) You pick Option A or B by EOD Monday 14-Sep.
2) We update the SOW with PS line if you want compressed schedule.
3) DocuSign route and procurement kickoff.

Best —
Karthik
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: pricing-options-20260913.csv, GlobalRetail-MAP-v2.xlsx (link in body)

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@globalretail.com>

Karthik —

We’ll take Option A (8% residency premium with 12-month commit and 90-day free failover). Please proceed to update the SOW to include the PS line for the compressed schedule and share the final DocuSign link. Procurement will expect SOC2 evidence and the DPA; procurement@globalretail.com will reach out with the standard contract redlines.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

–Elena
Elena Rossi
